collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE V: FAMILY DRAMA, FEUDS AND LEADERSHIP DISPUTES (LCE-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
All sorts of real-life drama suited to Isola: parents with opinions about who their children marry, arranged matches, inheritances, feuds between families, accusations, apologies that are not enough, and arguments about who should lead.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Two respected villagers both want to be the next leader: hold a village vote, or ask them to lead together.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The old {@chief} is stepping down, and the village has two candidates: (subject), who is bold and full of new ideas, and (friend), who is careful and knows every family's troubles. Each has their followers, and the arguing has spread to every cooking fire. How should the village decide?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: Every villager over sixteen drops a shell in one of two baskets. (friend) wins by eleven shells. (subject) congratulates (friend.him/her) publicly, then goes home and sulks for three days. Then (subject.he/she) comes to (friend) with a list of ideas. (friend) uses about half of them.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The village asks them to lead side by side. It is a disaster for the first month: they disagree about everything, in public. Then they work out a way: (subject) proposes, (friend) checks. The village grumbles that it takes twice as long to decide anything. It also makes fewer mistakes.
